props.title: Modular Play Equipment for Schools and Builders in India
props.summaryText: How modular play structures are put together, why they suit schools and real estate projects, and how to plan one that can grow with your budget.
props.author: rohan-mehta
props.imageAlt: Two children on swings at a modular playground in a school

takeaways.text: Modular play structures are built from standard towers, decks, links, slides and panels, combined to suit a site.
They let you fit irregular plots, match an age group and stay within a budget without a fully custom design.
Plan for expansion: leave space and agree the connection points so you can add towers later.
Standard parts make spares and repairs simpler for years.

faq.a: Modular playground equipment is built from standard components such as towers, platforms, steps, bridges, slides, climbers, roofs and play panels, which can be combined in different arrangements to suit a site, an age group and a budget.

faq.q: Can modular play equipment be extended later?
faq.a: Yes, if it is planned. Leave space within the layout, choose a design with connection points for extra towers or links, and keep the same range so parts match.

faq.q: Is modular play equipment good for schools?
faq.a: Yes. It can be arranged to fit the available space, sized for different age groups, extended in phases as budgets allow, and repaired with standard spare parts.
